questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding extratropical cyclones:
I. They usually develop in the mid and high latitudes.
II. They affect a much larger area as compared to tropical cyclone.
III. They move from east to west.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
Extratropical cyclones develop in the mid and high latitudes, beyond the tropics. Hence, statement I is correct.

They have a clear frontal system and cover a much larger area compared to tropical cyclones. Hence, statement II is correct.

Extratropical cyclones move from west to east under the influence of westerly winds, whereas tropical cyclones generally move from east to west. Hence, statement III is incorrect.

Therefore, only statements I and II are correct.

Answer: I and II only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Loose sediments are transformed into sedimentary rocks by the process of
questions.solution:
Lithification is the process by which loose, unconsolidated sediments are transformed into solid sedimentary rocks. This occurs through compaction, where the weight of overlying materials compresses the sediments, and cementation, where minerals precipitate from groundwater and bind the sediment particles together.

Weathering is the breakdown of rocks into smaller particles.

Mass wasting is the downward movement of rock and soil under gravity.

Solifluction is a specific type of mass wasting common in permafrost areas.

Answer: lithification

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Earthquake waves are basically of two types, namely body waves and surface waves.
II. The body waves interact with the surface rocks and generate surface waves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Earthquake waves are broadly classified into two types: body waves and surface waves. Body waves are generated due to the release of energy at the focus and move in all directions travelling through the body of the Earth.

When these body waves interact with the surface rocks, they generate a new set of waves called surface waves, which move along the surface.

Thus, both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is not a strategy in the Rainfed Area Development (RAD) scheme of India?
questions.solution:
Rainfed Area Development (RAD) is a component of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA).

The primary objective of RAD is to make rainfed agriculture more productive, sustainable, remunerative, and climate-resilient.

Key strategies of the RAD scheme include promoting Integrated Farming Systems (diversified farming), soil health management, and adopting a cluster-based approach to maximize the impact of interventions.

Since rainfed areas primarily depend on rainfall and lack assured irrigation, optimizing canal irrigation is not a strategy under the RAD scheme. It is typically a focus of command area development programs for irrigated regions.

Answer: Optimizing canal irrigation

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: As per the land-use categories in the Land Revenue Records of India, 'a cultivable land which is left uncultivated for more than a year but less than 5 years' is called
questions.solution:
According to the land-use categories in the Land Revenue Records of India:

Current fallow is the land left uncultivated for one agricultural year or less.

Fallow other than current fallow is the cultivable land which is left uncultivated for more than a year but less than 5 years.

Culturable wasteland is the land left uncultivated for more than 5 years.

Barren and unculturable land is the land which cannot be brought under cultivation except at an exorbitant cost.

Therefore, the given description corresponds to fallow, other than current fallow.

Answer: fallow, other than current fallow

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about temperature inversion:
I. This happens when normal lapse rate gets inverted.
II. Winter nights with cloudy skies are conducive for temperature inversion.
III. Polar areas experience inversion throughout the year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
Temperature inversion is a reversal of the normal behavior of temperature in the troposphere, where a layer of cool air at the surface is overlain by a layer of warmer air. Under normal conditions, temperature usually decreases with height, which is known as the normal lapse rate. When this is reversed, the normal lapse rate gets inverted. Thus, Statement I is correct.

Ideal conditions for temperature inversion include long winter nights, clear skies, calm air, and dry air. Cloudy skies prevent the rapid cooling of the earth's surface by trapping outgoing terrestrial radiation, which hinders the formation of a temperature inversion. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

In polar regions, due to the extremely cold surface, temperature inversion is a normal phenomenon that occurs throughout the year. Thus, Statement III is correct.

Therefore, only statements I and III are correct.

Answer: I and III only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Types of Chemical WeatheringCharacteristics
I. SolutionResults in leaching of minerals
II. CarbonationHelps in breaking down feldspars
III. HydrationCauses an increase in the volume of rocks
IV. OxidationChanges the colour of rocks

How many pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
Chemical weathering processes include solution, carbonation, hydration, and oxidation.

I. Solution involves the dissolution of soluble minerals in water or weak acids, leading to the leaching of minerals from rocks. This pair is correctly matched.

II. Carbonation is the reaction of carbonates and bicarbonates with minerals. It is a common process that helps in the breaking down of feldspars and carbonate minerals. This pair is correctly matched.

III. Hydration is the chemical addition of water. Minerals absorb water and expand, causing an increase in the volume of the rocks, which leads to physical stress. This pair is correctly matched.

IV. Oxidation involves the reaction of minerals with oxygen to form oxides or hydroxides. This process often changes the colour of rocks, such as iron-bearing minerals turning red, brown, or yellow upon oxidation. This pair is correctly matched.

All four pairs are correctly matched.

Answer: All the four

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. In a seismograph, P waves are recorded earlier than S waves.
II. In P waves, the individual particles vibrate to and fro in the direction of wave propagation whereas in S waves, the particles vibrate up and down at right angles to the direction of wave propagation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
P waves are primary waves and travel faster than S waves. Thus, they reach the seismograph first and are recorded earlier. Statement I is correct.

P waves are longitudinal waves, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate to and fro parallel to the direction of wave propagation. S waves are transverse waves, meaning the particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation. Statement II is correct.

Both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding hypocentre:
I. It is the point where the energy is released and is called the focus of an earthquake.
II. It is the point where the earthquake starts and may be many kilometers deep within the Earth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The hypocentre is the point within the Earth where an earthquake rupture starts. It is also commonly termed the focus.

It is the exact location where the strain energy stored in the rock is first released, marking the origin of the seismic waves.

This point can be located at various depths beneath the Earth's surface, ranging from near the surface to hundreds of kilometers deep.

Thus, both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following critical minerals:
I. Neodymium
II. Tellurium
III. Dysprosium
IV. Gallium
Which of the above minerals are not used for the production of photovoltaic cells used in solar panels?
questions.solution:
Neodymium (I) and Dysprosium (III) are rare earth elements primarily used in the manufacturing of strong permanent magnets, which are essential for wind turbines and electric vehicle motors. They are not used in the production of photovoltaic cells.

Tellurium (II) is a key component in cadmium telluride (CdTe) thin-film solar cells.

Gallium (IV) is used in the production of copper indium gallium selenide (CIGS) and gallium arsenide (GaAs) solar cells.

Thus, Neodymium and Dysprosium are not used for the production of photovoltaic cells.

Answer: I and III

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following winds is responsible for wildfires in Southern California?
questions.solution:
Santa Ana winds are strong, extremely dry down-slope winds that originate inland and affect coastal Southern California and northern Baja California. They are notorious for exacerbating regional wildfires due to their dry and warm nature.

Diablo winds and Jarbo Gap winds affect Northern California, while Chinook winds occur in the interior West of North America (Rocky Mountains).

Answer: Santa Ana wind

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Mount Ibu, which recently erupted in Indonesia, is a
questions.solution:
Mount Ibu is a stratovolcano, which is also known as a composite volcano. It is located on the northwest coast of Halmahera island in Indonesia.

Composite volcanoes are conical volcanoes built up by many layers (strata) of hardened lava, tephra, pumice, and volcanic ash.

Answer: composite volcano

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements in case of terrestrial planets:
I. Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are terrestrial planets having low densities as compared to other planets.
II. They lie between the Sun and the belt of asteroids.
III. Their lower gravity can hold the escaping gases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is incorrect because terrestrial planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars) are primarily composed of rock and metal and have high densities compared to the Jovian planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune), which are gas giants with much lower densities.

Statement II is correct. The terrestrial planets are the inner planets, and their orbits lie between the Sun and the asteroid belt.

Statement III is correct. Because the terrestrial planets are smaller, they have lower gravity compared to the Jovian planets. This lower gravity is insufficient to hold escaping gases, which is why they do not possess thick, massive atmospheres of light gases like hydrogen and helium, unlike the giant outer planets.

Therefore, statements II and III are correct.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Layers of AtmosphereCharacteristics
I. TroposphereAbsorbs ultraviolet radiation
II. StratosphereChanges in weather and climate
III. MesosphereReflects radio waves back to the Earth

How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere where all changes in weather and climate take place. The given characteristic for the troposphere is incorrect.

The stratosphere contains the ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun. The given characteristic for the stratosphere is incorrect.

The ionosphere (a part of the thermosphere) contains electrically charged particles called ions, which reflect radio waves back to the Earth. The mesosphere is the layer where meteors burn up upon entering the atmosphere. The given characteristic for the mesosphere is incorrect.

Since all three pairs are incorrectly matched, none of the pairs are correct.

Answer: None

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
BooksAuthors
I. DayabhagaJimutavahana
II. Prithviraj RasoChandbardai
III. LilavatiBhaskaracharya
IV. MitaksharaVijnaneshvara

How many pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
Dayabhaga is a Hindu law treatise written by Jimutavahana.

Prithviraj Raso is an epic poem about the life of Prithviraj Chauhan, written by Chandbardai.

Lilavati is a treatise on mathematics written by the Indian mathematician Bhaskaracharya (Bhaskara II).

Mitakshara is a legal commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti, written by Vijnaneshvara.

All four pairs are correctly matched.

Answer: All the four

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order from the earliest to recent:
I. British East India Company formed
II. Magellan circumnavigated the globe
III. Dutch East India Company formed
IV. Vasco da Gama reached Calicut/Kozhikode
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in $1498$.

Magellan's expedition circumnavigated the globe between $1519$ and $1522$.

The British East India Company was formed in $1600$.

The Dutch East India Company was formed in $1602$.

The correct chronological order is IV, II, I, III.

Answer: IV, II, I, III

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
InventionsInventors
I. Flying shuttle loomJohn Kay
II. Water frameJames Hargreaves
III. Spinning jennyRichard Arkwright

How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The flying shuttle loom was invented by John Kay in 1733. Thus, pair I is correctly matched.

The water frame was invented by Richard Arkwright in 1769. Thus, pair II is incorrectly matched.

The spinning jenny was invented by James Hargreaves in 1764. Thus, pair III is incorrectly matched.

Only one pair is correctly matched.

Answer: One

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of the Rowlatt Act of 1919:
I. Gandhiji launched a nationwide Satyagraha against the proposed Rowlatt Act, 1919.
II. The Act had been hurriedly passed through the Imperial Legislative Council despite the opposition of Indian members.
III. The Act gave the Government enormous powers to repress political activities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The Rowlatt Act (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919) was hurriedly passed by the Imperial Legislative Council despite the united opposition of the Indian members. This makes Statement II correct.

The Act gave the government enormous powers to repress political activities and allowed the detention of political prisoners without trial for two years. This makes Statement III correct.

In response to this unjust law, Mahatma Gandhi decided to launch a nationwide Satyagraha, which started with a hartal on 6 April 1919. This makes Statement I correct.

Since all three statements are correct, the correct option includes I, II, and III.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Industrial Revolution in Britain:
I. There was availability of banks which could loan money to set up industries.
II. There was a good transport network.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The Industrial Revolution in Britain was facilitated by several key factors.

Statement I is correct. Britain had a well-developed financial system. The Bank of England was established in 1694, and by the late eighteenth century, there were numerous provincial banks that provided the necessary capital and loans to entrepreneurs to set up industries.

Statement II is also correct. Britain possessed an excellent transport network. It had a long coastline and many navigable rivers, which made the transportation of raw materials and finished goods easier and cheaper. This was later enhanced by the construction of canals and railways.

Since both statements are correct, the correct option is Both I and II.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Russian Revolution:
I. The incident known as 'Bloody Sunday' started a series of events known as the 1905 Revolution.
II. Lawyers, doctors, engineers and other middle-class workers established the Union of Unions and demanded a Constituent Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The incident of 'Bloody Sunday' occurred in 1905 when a peaceful procession of workers led by Father Gapon was attacked by the police and the Cossacks, resulting in the death of over 100 workers. This event triggered a series of strikes and protests across the country, which came to be known as the 1905 Revolution.

During the 1905 Revolution, various sections of society, including lawyers, doctors, engineers, and other middle-class workers, formed the Union of Unions. They actively participated in the protests and demanded the establishment of a Constituent Assembly to draft a constitution for Russia.

Both statements are historically accurate.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Who among the following advocated the construction of initial railways in India for facilitating army movement?
questions.solution:
Lord Dalhousie, who served as the Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856, is widely regarded as the 'Father of Indian Railways'. In his famous Railway Minute of 1853, he strongly advocated for the construction of a network of railways in India. His primary motivations were to facilitate the rapid movement of the British army to maintain control over the vast Indian territory and to promote British commercial interests by enabling the easy transport of raw materials from the interior to the ports and manufactured goods from the ports to the interior markets.

Answer: Lord Dalhousie

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which of the following are associated with composite volcanoes?
I. They result in explosive eruptions.
II. They eject pyroclastic materials.
III. Pyroclastic materials and ashes accumulate near the vent, forming layers.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
Composite volcanoes are characterised by eruptions of cooler and more viscous lavas than basalt. These volcanoes often result in explosive eruptions.

Along with lava, large quantities of pyroclastic material and ashes find their way to the ground.

This material gathers near the vent openings leading to the creation of layers, which gives them the name composite volcanoes or stratovolcanoes.

Therefore, all three statements I, II, and III are correct.

Answer: I, II and III

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The large well supplying water to the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro was located
options: near the drain of the tank
at the top of one of the staircases
in one of the adjoining rooms on the eastern side
at the bottom of the tank in a corner
questions.solution:
The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro was a large rectangular tank in a courtyard surrounded by a corridor. There were rooms on three sides of the Great Bath. In one of the adjoining rooms on the eastern side, there was a large well that supplied water to the tank.

Water from the tank was drained out through a huge drain.

Answer: in one of the adjoining rooms on the eastern side

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Earth's crust:
I. The continental crust is thinner under fold mountains.
II. The mean thickness of ocean crust is $30\,\text{km}$.
III. The Earth's crust is brittle in nature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is incorrect. The continental crust is thicker in the areas of major mountain systems. For example, it is about $70\,\text{km}$ thick in the Himalayan region.

Statement II is incorrect. The mean thickness of the oceanic crust is about $5\,\text{km}$, whereas that of the continental crust is around $30\,\text{km}$.

Statement III is correct. The Earth's crust is the outermost solid part of the Earth and is brittle in nature, meaning it is prone to fracturing and faulting under stress.

Therefore, only statement III is correct.

Answer: III only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
If you like to visit famous Jain pilgrimage sites, which of the following towns you will have to travel to?
I. Moodabidri
II. Madurai
III. Sonagiri
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
Moodabidri, located in Karnataka, is renowned as the 'Jain Kashi' of the South due to its numerous Jain basadis, most notably the Saavira Kambada Basadi (Thousand Pillars Temple). Thus, it is a famous Jain pilgrimage site.

Madurai, located in Tamil Nadu, while predominantly known for the Meenakshi Amman Temple (a Hindu site), also has significant historical connections to Jainism. There are several Jain caves and rock beds containing ancient inscriptions and carvings of Tirthankaras in the hills surrounding Madurai, such as Samanar Hills, indicating it was an important Jain center in antiquity.

Sonagiri, located in Madhya Pradesh, is a highly revered Digambara Jain pilgrimage site, known for its numerous white temples scattered across the hills, marking the place where many ascetics achieved salvation.

Therefore, all three towns are associated with significant Jain pilgrimage or historical sites.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Kamarajar Port:
I. It is an example of corporatized public company.
II. It was earlier known as Ennore Port.
III. It is a natural port.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
Kamarajar Port, formerly known as Ennore Port, is the 12th major port of India.

It is the first corporatized major port in India and is registered as a public company.

It is an artificial port, not a natural port.

Thus, statements I and II are correct, while statement III is incorrect.

Answer: I and II only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Quartzite is metamorphosed from which one of the following rocks?
questions.solution:
Quartzite is a hard, non-foliated metamorphic rock which was originally pure quartz sandstone.

Sandstone is converted into quartzite through heating and pressure usually related to tectonic compression within orogenic belts.

Limestone metamorphoses into marble, while shale metamorphoses into slate, phyllite, schist, or gneiss.

Answer: Sandstone

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following receives an average annual rainfall of below $50\,\text{cm}$ in India, indicating highest inadequacy?
questions.solution:
Ladakh is a cold desert located in the rain shadow region of the Great Himalayas. The Himalayan mountains block the monsoon clouds from reaching this region.

As a result, Ladakh receives an extremely low average annual rainfall of less than $10\,\text{cm}$, which is well below $50\,\text{cm}$. This indicates the highest inadequacy of rainfall among the given options.

Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand receive moderate to high rainfall, while Haryana receives around $40\,\text{cm}$ to $60\,\text{cm}$ of rainfall annually.

Answer: Ladakh

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Second Five-Year Plan sought to promote development which would establish socialistic pattern of society in India.
II. Between 1966 and 1969, three Annual Plans were formulated.
III. The Ninth Five-Year Plan could not take off at its stipulated time in the 60th year of India's Independence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct. The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961) was based on the Mahalanobis model and aimed at establishing a socialistic pattern of society, following the resolution passed at the Avadi session of the Indian National Congress in 1955.

Statement II is correct. The period between 1966 and 1969 is known as the Plan Holiday. Due to the Indo-Pak war, drought, and inflation, the Fourth Five-Year Plan was postponed, and three Annual Plans were formulated during this period.

Statement III is incorrect. The Eighth Five-Year Plan (not the Ninth) could not take off at its stipulated time in 1990 due to political instability at the centre, leading to two Annual Plans for 1990-91 and 1991-92. The Ninth Five-Year Plan was launched on schedule in 1997, which marked the 50th year of India's Independence, not the 60th.

Therefore, only statements I and II are correct.

Answer: I and II only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India:
I. The CAG shall be appointed by the President of India.
II. The CAG is not eligible for further office under the Government of India after he has ceased to hold his office.
III. The reports of the CAG relating to the accounts of the Union shall be submitted to the Prime Minister who shall cause them to be laid before the House of the People.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
According to Article 148(1) of the Constitution of India, the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal. Thus, Statement I is correct.

According to Article 148(4), the CAG is not eligible for further office either under the Government of India or under the Government of any State after ceasing to hold office. Thus, Statement II is correct.

According to Article 151(1), the reports of the CAG relating to the accounts of the Union are submitted to the President, who causes them to be laid before each House of Parliament, not the Prime Minister. Thus, Statement III is incorrect.

Therefore, only statements I and II are correct.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements with regard to bead production in Harappan towns:
I. The materials used to make beads included carnelian, quartz and steatite.
II. The beads were cylindrical, barrel-shaped and disc-shaped.
III. Specialized stone drills were used for making holes through the beads.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The materials used to make beads in Harappan towns included stones like carnelian, jasper, crystal, quartz, and steatite, as well as metals like copper, bronze, and gold, and materials like shell, faience, and terracotta.

The shapes of the beads were numerous, including disc-shaped, cylindrical, spherical, barrel-shaped, and segmented.

Specialized drills used for making holes through the beads have been found at archaeological sites such as Chanhudaro, Lothal, and Dholavira.

Therefore, all the given statements are correct.

Answer: I, II and III

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following offices:
I. The Vice President of India
II. The Governors within their respective States
III. The Prime Minister of India
IV. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Which one of the following options represents the correct order of these offices for ceremonial occasions in the Table of Precedence as approved by the President of India?
questions.solution:
According to the Table of Precedence of the Republic of India, the order of precedence is as follows:

Rank $1$: President of India
Rank $2$: Vice President of India (I)
Rank $3$: Prime Minister of India (III)
Rank $4$: Governors of States within their respective States (II)
Rank $5$: Former Presidents
Rank $5$A: Deputy Prime Minister
Rank $6$: Chief Justice of India, Speaker of the Lok Sabha (IV)

Thus, the correct order of precedence for the given offices is Vice President of India, Prime Minister of India, Governors within their respective States, and Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

The correct sequence is I, III, II, IV.

Answer: I, III, II, IV

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following pairs:
I. Part IX AThe Municipalities
II. Part IX BThe Cooperative Societies
III. Part XRelations between the Union and States
IV. Part XIIFinance, Property, Contracts and Suits

How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
Part IX A of the Constitution of India deals with The Municipalities. This pair is correctly matched.

Part IX B of the Constitution of India deals with The Cooperative Societies. This pair is correctly matched.

Part X of the Constitution of India deals with The Scheduled and Tribal Areas, whereas Relations between the Union and the States are covered under Part XI. This pair is incorrectly matched.

Part XII of the Constitution of India deals with Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits. This pair is correctly matched.

Three pairs are correctly matched.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: As per Article 324 of the Constitution of India, the Chief Election Commissioner shall not be removed from his office except in like manner and on the like grounds as
options: a Judge of the Supreme Court
a Judge of a High Court
the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.solution:
According to Article 324(5) of the Constitution of India, the Chief Election Commissioner shall not be removed from his office except in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

This provision ensures the independence of the Election Commission by providing security of tenure to the Chief Election Commissioner.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Constitution of India mentions that the Speaker has the power to adjourn both the Houses sine die.
II. On prorogation, it is only the Speaker who can summon the Houses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is incorrect because the Speaker is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha and has the power to adjourn only the Lok Sabha sine die. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha has the power to adjourn the Rajya Sabha sine die. The Speaker does not have the power to adjourn both Houses.

Statement II is incorrect because under Article 85(1) of the Constitution of India, it is the President who has the power to summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit, not the Speaker.

Therefore, neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct.

Answer: Neither I nor II

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is not a pass of Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
Muling La is located in Uttarakhand and connects it with Tibet.

Kumjawng Pass, Yonggyap Pass, and Bomdi La are all located in Arunachal Pradesh.

Therefore, Muling La is not a pass of Arunachal Pradesh.

Answer: Muling La

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: PM MITRA Parks relate to which one of the following industries?
questions.solution:
PM MITRA stands for PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel.

The PM MITRA Parks scheme is an initiative by the Government of India aimed at developing the textile sector by creating world-class infrastructure, attracting investments, and boosting employment and exports in the textile industry.

Answer: Textile

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one among the following Departments is not under the Ministry of Home Affairs?
options: The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
questions.solution:
The Ministry of Home Affairs consists of six departments:
1. Department of Border Management
2. Department of Internal Security
3. Department of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh Affairs
4. Department of Home
5. Department of Official Language
6. Department of States

The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation comes under the Ministry of Jal Shakti. Therefore, it is not under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Answer: The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one amongst the following cities has been designated as the UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy in 2025?
questions.solution:
Indore has been nominated/designated to compete for the UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy tag for the year 2025. The city is renowned for its rich culinary heritage, vibrant street food culture, and iconic food hubs like Chappan Dukan and Sarafa Bazaar, which have also received recognition from FSSAI.

Answer: Indore

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following countries became the 11th member of ASEAN in 2025?
questions.solution:
ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) was established in 1967. The original members were Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand.

Brunei joined in 1984, Vietnam in 1995, Laos and Myanmar in 1997, and Cambodia in 1999, making it a 10-member bloc.

Timor-Leste was admitted in principle as the 11th member of ASEAN and is the newest country to join the regional bloc.

Answer: Timor-Leste

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Choose the correct set of the following cities in descending order (according to the Degree of Urbanization definitions in 2025) in terms of population.
options: Tokyo, Dhaka, Manila, New Delhi, Jakarta
Jakarta, Dhaka, Tokyo, New Delhi, Manila
Tokyo, Manila, Dhaka, Jakarta, New Delhi
Jakarta, Tokyo, Dhaka, New Delhi, Manila
questions.solution:
According to the Degree of Urbanization (DEGURBA) methodology, which defines cities based on contiguous high-density grid cells (Urban Centres), population rankings differ from traditional metropolitan area definitions.

Under this definition, Jakarta forms a massive continuous high-density urban centre, making its population larger than Tokyo's. The projected descending order of population for these urban centres in 2025 is:

1. Jakarta
2. Tokyo
3. Dhaka
4. New Delhi
5. Manila

Thus, the correct sequence is Jakarta, Tokyo, Dhaka, New Delhi, Manila.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following countries:
I. Haiti
II. Philippines
III. Nicaragua
IV. India
According to the Climate Risk Index 2026, which of the above countries were affected by recurring extreme events during 1995-2024?
questions.solution:
The Global Climate Risk Index analyzes the extent to which countries have been affected by weather-related loss events such as storms, floods, and heatwaves.

Haiti and Nicaragua are highly vulnerable to recurrent hurricanes and extreme weather events in their respective regions.

The Philippines is located in the Pacific typhoon belt, making it highly susceptible to frequent and severe typhoons.

India consistently faces recurring extreme events including severe monsoon floods, cyclones, and heatwaves, placing it among the countries most affected by long-term climate risks.

Therefore, according to climate risk indices assessing long-term vulnerability, all the listed countries namely Haiti, Philippines, Nicaragua, and India have been significantly affected by recurring extreme weather events.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which of the following main industry/industries was/were developed in the second industrial revolution that took place after about 1850?
questions.solution:
The first industrial revolution, which began in the late 18th century, was primarily based on coal, iron, steam engines, and the mechanization of the textile industry (cotton spinning and weaving).

The second industrial revolution, which took place after about 1850, was characterized by rapid industrialization and the development of new industries such as steel, chemicals, electricity, and petroleum.

Therefore, the chemical and electrical industries were the main industries developed during the second industrial revolution.

Answer: Chemical and electrical

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which among the following materials was used in making the Harappan seals?
questions.solution:
Harappan seals were predominantly made of steatite, which is a soft stone. Its softness allowed for intricate carving of animal motifs and the Indus script.

Answer: Steatite

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one among the following mahajanapadas in ancient India was an oligarchy?
questions.solution:
In ancient India, the Mahajanapadas were broadly divided into monarchies and republics (or oligarchies).

Magadha, Kosala, and Gandhara were ruled by kings and had a monarchical system of government.

Vajji (or Vrijji) was a confederacy of eight clans, the most prominent among them being the Licchavis, Videhans, Jnatrikas, and Vajjis. It was governed by an assembly of clan heads, making it an oligarchy or a republic (Gana-Sangha).

Answer : Vajji

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following sculptures found at Sanchi Stupa is NOT directly inspired by Buddhist ideas?
questions.solution:
The sculptures at Sanchi Stupa include various symbols that represent the Buddha and his teachings. The empty seat indicates the meditation of the Buddha, the tree symbolizes his enlightenment, and the wheel stands for his first sermon. These are directly inspired by Buddhist ideas.

The Shalbhanjika motif, which depicts a woman holding a tree branch, is derived from popular pre-Buddhist beliefs. According to these beliefs, her touch caused trees to flower and bear fruit. This auspicious symbol was incorporated into Buddhist art but was not directly inspired by Buddhist ideas.

Answer: Shalbhanjika

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: In British India, which one among the following Acts permitted detention without trial for up to two years?
questions.solution:
The Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919, popularly known as the Rowlatt Act, was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in Delhi. It authorized the British government to arrest any person suspected of anti-government activities and detain them without trial for up to two years.

Answer: Rowlatt Act, 1919

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Bhoodan Movement is correct?
options: The target was to get one-sixth of cultivable land in India as donation
It was approved through a Central Government Act
It was ensured that the donated land was free from all litigation
The first donation of land was in Bihar
questions.solution:
The Bhoodan Movement was initiated by Acharya Vinoba Bhave in 1951 at Pochampally village in Telangana (then part of Hyderabad State). Thus, the first donation of land was not in Bihar.

The movement was a voluntary land reform initiative, and Vinoba Bhave appealed to landowners to consider him as their sixth son and donate one-sixth of their cultivable land for distribution among the landless. The target was to collect 50 million acres, which was roughly one-sixth of India's total cultivable land at the time.

The movement was not approved through a Central Government Act; rather, various state governments later passed their own Bhoodan Acts to facilitate the legal transfer of donated lands.

A significant portion of the donated land was either uncultivable or entangled in legal disputes, meaning it was not ensured that the donated land was free from litigation.

Therefore, the only correct statement is that the target was to get one-sixth of the cultivable land in India as a donation.

Answer: The target was to get one-sixth of cultivable land in India as donation

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act provides for
options: an elaborate system of establishing municipal self-government
an elaborate system of establishing panchayats as units of self-government
establishing a Commission for Linguistic Minorities
the creation of the Jharkhand State
questions.solution:
art IX to the Constitution consisting of 16 Articles and the Eleventh Schedule. It provides for an elaborate system of establishing panchayats as units of local self-government in rural areas.

The Seventy-fourth Amendment Act deals with municipalities (urban local government).

Answer: an elaborate system of establishing panchayats as units of self-government

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: BHARATPOL portal has been developed by
options: The Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.solution:
The BHARATPOL portal has been developed by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). It serves as a national platform for sharing information and intelligence among various law enforcement agencies in India.

Answer: The Central Bureau of Investigation

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Parliament of India is correct?
options: A majority of members of Rajya Sabha are elected by a system of proportional representation by means of single transferable vote
The Deputy Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha is nominated by the President from among the members of the Rajya Sabha
The Lok Sabha cannot be dissolved before the completion of its five year term
The members of Lok Sabha also vote in the election of the members of Rajya Sabha
questions.solution:
The Rajya Sabha consists of a maximum of $250$ members, out of which $238$ members are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies. The election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. The remaining $12$ members are nominated by the President. Thus, a majority of the members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by this system.

The Deputy Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha is elected by the members of the Rajya Sabha from amongst themselves, not nominated by the President.

The Lok Sabha can be dissolved by the President before the completion of its five-year term on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

The members of the Lok Sabha do not vote in the election of the members of the Rajya Sabha; only the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies do.

Answer: A majority of members of Rajya Sabha are elected by a system of proportional representation by means of single transferable vote

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following pairs related to the United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goals:
I. Goal 1End poverty in all forms everywhere
II. Goal 2Ensure healthy lives
III. Goal 3Ensure quality education
IV. Goal 4Achieve gender equality

How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are as follows:

Goal 1: End poverty in all its forms everywhere.

Goal 2: End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture.

Goal 3: Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages.

Goal 4: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all.

Goal 5: Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls.

From the given pairs, only Goal 1 is correctly matched. Goal 2 is Zero Hunger, Goal 3 is Good Health and Well-being, and Goal 4 is Quality Education.

Therefore, only one pair is correctly matched.

Answer: One

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Maize (makka) was introduced into India in the seventeenth century via
questions.solution:
Maize (makka) is native to the Americas and was introduced into India by the Portuguese in the seventeenth century. The Portuguese were responsible for bringing several New World crops to India, including maize, potatoes, tomatoes, tobacco, and chillies.

Answer: Portugal

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one among the following does NOT figure among the Five Principles of Panchsheel?
options: Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty
questions.solution:
The Five Principles of Panchsheel (Peaceful Coexistence) are:
1. Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty.
2. Mutual non-aggression.
3. Mutual non-interference in each other's internal affairs.
4. Equality and mutual benefit.
5. Peaceful co-existence.

Nuclear non-proliferation is not a part of the Panchsheel principles.

Answer: Nuclear non-proliferation

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about Srimanta Shankardeva is/are correct?
1. In the late fifteenth century Shankardeva emerged as one of the leading proponents of Vaishnavism in Assam
2. He was the founder of Gaudiya Vaishnavism
3. His teachings are known as Bhagavati Dharma
4. He encouraged the establishment of satra and naam ghar

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
Srimanta Shankardeva was a 15th-16th century Assamese polymath, saint-scholar, and socio-religious reformer. He emerged as one of the leading proponents of Vaishnavism in Assam in the late fifteenth century. Thus, statement 1 is correct.

Gaudiya Vaishnavism was founded by Chaitanya Mahaprabhu in Bengal, not by Shankardeva. Shankardeva founded the Ekasarana Dharma. Thus, statement 2 is incorrect.

His teachings are based on the Bhagavad Gita and the Bhagavata Purana, and are widely known as Bhagavati Dharma or Ekasarana Dharma. Thus, statement 3 is correct.

He encouraged the establishment of Satras (monasteries) and Naam Ghars (prayer halls) for the propagation of his teachings and community worship. Thus, statement 4 is correct.

Statements 1, 3, and 4 are correct.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
With reference to the United Nations (UN), consider the following pairs:
United Nations Peacekeeping OperationsCountries
I. UNMOGIPIndia and Pakistan
II. UNFICYPCyprus
III. UNMIKKosovo
IV. UNTSOHaiti

How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
UNMOGIP stands for United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan. It was established to observe the ceasefire in Jammu and Kashmir. Pair I is correctly matched.

UNFICYP stands for United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus. It was established to prevent further fighting between the Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot communities. Pair II is correctly matched.

UNMIK stands for United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo. It was established to provide an interim administration for Kosovo. Pair III is correctly matched.

UNTSO stands for United Nations Truce Supervision Organization. It was established in the Middle East to monitor ceasefires and supervise armistice agreements, not in Haiti. Pair IV is incorrectly matched.

Three pairs are correctly matched.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Match List I with List II and select the answer using the code given below the Lists:
List I (Five Year Plan)List II (Objective)
A. Fifth Five Year Plan1. Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth
B. Seventh Five Year Plan2. Garibi Hatao (Removal of Poverty)
C. Ninth Five Year Plan3. Food, Work and Productivity
D. Eleventh Five Year Plan4. Growth with Social Justice and Equality
questions.solution:
The Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-1979) focused on poverty alleviation (Garibi Hatao) and self-reliance.

The Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-1990) emphasized policies and programs that would accelerate the growth in foodgrains production, increase employment opportunities, and raise productivity (Food, Work and Productivity).

The Ninth Five Year Plan (1997-2002) was launched with the primary objective of Growth with Social Justice and Equality.

The Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-2012) had the central theme of Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth.

Thus, the correct matching is A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1.

Answer: A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. A Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
II. The Rajya Sabha has no power to reject a Money Bill but can suggest amendment(s).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
According to Article 109(1) of the Constitution of India, a Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha). Thus, Statement I is correct.

According to Article 109(2), after a Money Bill has been passed by the House of the People (Lok Sabha), it is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha for its recommendations. The Rajya Sabha has no power to reject or amend a Money Bill directly. It can only return the bill within a period of fourteen days with its recommendations (suggested amendments), which the Lok Sabha may either accept or reject. Thus, Statement II is also correct.

Both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
With reference to the territorial jurisdictions of High Courts in India, consider the following pairs:
High CourtsTerritorial Jurisdictions
I. Calcutta High CourtLakshadweep
II. Madras High CourtPuducherry
III. Gauhati High CourtManipur
IV. Kerala High CourtAndaman and Nicobar Islands

How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The Calcutta High Court has territorial jurisdiction over West Bengal and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Lakshadweep comes under the jurisdiction of the Kerala High Court. Thus, Pair I is incorrectly matched.

The Madras High Court has territorial jurisdiction over Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. Thus, Pair II is correctly matched.

The Gauhati High Court has territorial jurisdiction over Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, and Arunachal Pradesh. Manipur has its own High Court, established in $2013$. Thus, Pair III is incorrectly matched.

The Kerala High Court has territorial jurisdiction over Kerala and Lakshadweep. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands come under the jurisdiction of the Calcutta High Court. Thus, Pair IV is incorrectly matched.

Only one pair is correctly matched.

Answer: One

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
With reference to defence cooperation between India and Russia, which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. BrahMos Cruise Missile system is jointly developed by India's DRDO and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya (NPOM).
II. The production site of the Indo-Russia Rifles Private Limited (IRRPL) joint venture is in Korwa, Madhya Pradesh under the 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' initiative.
Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct. The BrahMos Cruise Missile system is a joint venture between India's Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya (NPOM).

Statement II is incorrect. The Indo-Russia Rifles Private Limited (IRRPL) is a joint venture to manufacture AK-203 assault rifles, but its production facility is located at the Korwa Ordnance Factory in Amethi district, Uttar Pradesh, not Madhya Pradesh.

Therefore, only Statement I is correct.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: At which one among the following places did the British East India Company found its factory in the year 1611?
questions.solution:
The British East India Company established its first factory in the south at Masulipatam (Machilipatnam) on the Coromandel Coast in the year 1611.

Later, in 1613, they established their first permanent factory at Surat after obtaining permission from the Mughal Emperor Jahangir.

Answer: Masulipatam

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) is set up by the
options: Department of Science and Technology, Government of India
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India
Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
questions.solution:
The Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) is a flagship initiative set up by the NITI Aayog to promote innovation and entrepreneurship across the length and breadth of the country.

Its objective is to create a facilitating environment for transformation of ideas into innovative and impactful solutions at schools, universities, research institutions, MSME and industry levels across the country.

Answer: NITI Aayog

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which among the following Acts provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court of Justice at Calcutta for Europeans, their employees and the citizens of India?
questions.solution:
The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first major step taken by the British Parliament to control and regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.

It provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William, Calcutta, which was established in 1774. It comprised one chief justice and three other judges.

This court had jurisdiction over Europeans, their employees, and the citizens of Calcutta.

Answer: The Regulating Act of 1773

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Who, among the following, has introduced a resolution in 1882 which is also called the Magna Carta of Local Self-Government in India?
questions.solution:
Lord Ripon introduced the Resolution of 1882, which is widely regarded as the Magna Carta of Local Self-Government in India. This resolution laid the foundation for the development of local self-government institutions in the country, emphasizing the importance of political education and the involvement of Indians in administration.

Answer: Lord Ripon

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Who among the following is the winner of the 2024-2025 Ranji Trophy?
questions.solution:
The Ranji Trophy is a premier domestic first-class cricket championship played in India.

Vidarbha emerged as the winner of the 2024-2025 edition of the Ranji Trophy tournament.

Answer: Vidarbha

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which of the following is the correct ascending order of the given minerals in terms of their presence in the Earth's crust?
1. Amphibolite
2. Mica
3. Pyroxene

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
According to the mineral composition of the Earth's crust:

Mica constitutes about $4\%$ of the Earth's crust.

Amphibole constitutes about $7\%$ of the Earth's crust.

Pyroxene constitutes about $10\%$ of the Earth's crust.

The correct ascending order of their presence in the Earth's crust is Mica, Amphibole, and Pyroxene. This corresponds to the sequence 2, 1, 3.

Answer: 2, 1, 3

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following features:
1. Consent of the governed
2. Political equality
3. Accountability of the ruled to the ruler

Which of the above feature/features outline democratic rule?
questions.solution:
Democracy is a form of government in which the rulers are elected by the people. The fundamental principles of democratic rule include the consent of the governed, meaning the government's legitimacy and moral right to use state power is justified and lawful only when consented to by the people or society over which that political power is exercised.

Political equality is another core feature, ensuring that all citizens have an equal voice in the political process, typically expressed as 'one person, one vote'.

In a democracy, the rulers (government) are accountable to the ruled (citizens), not the other way around. The statement 'Accountability of the ruled to the ruler' contradicts democratic principles and is a feature of authoritarian regimes.

Therefore, only features 1 and 2 outline democratic rule.

Answer: 1 and 2 only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Placing the earliest first, arrange the following countries in the chronological order in which they granted universal adult franchise:
1. USA
2. Sri Lanka
3. Japan
4. India

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
The chronological order in which the given countries granted universal adult franchise is as follows:

Sri Lanka granted universal adult franchise in $1931$ under the Donoughmore Constitution.

Japan granted universal adult franchise in $1945$ after the end of World War II.

India granted universal adult franchise in $1950$ when the Constitution of India came into effect.

The United States of America granted true universal adult franchise in $1965$ with the passing of the Voting Rights Act, which removed discriminatory barriers that prevented African Americans from voting.

Therefore, the correct chronological order is Sri Lanka (1931$), Japan (1945$), India (1950$), and USA (1965$), which corresponds to the sequence $2, 3, 4, 1$.

Answer: 2, 3, 4, 1

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which of the following is/are the applied forces in mechanical weathering process?
1. Gravitational force
2. Expansion force
3. Force due to water pressure

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
Mechanical weathering processes depend on applied forces which cause the physical breakdown of rocks without changing their chemical composition.

These applied forces include:
1. Gravitational forces such as overburden pressure, load, and shearing stress.
2. Expansion forces due to temperature changes, crystal growth, or animal activity.
3. Water pressures controlled by wetting and drying cycles.

Hence, all the given forces are applied forces in the mechanical weathering process.

Answer: 1, 2 and 3

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following lines of Longitude and Latitude:
1. Prime Meridian
2. Tropic of Cancer
3. Equator

Which of the above lines is/are a Great Circle?
questions.solution:
A great circle is a circle on the surface of a sphere which lies in a plane passing through the sphere's center. It divides the Earth into two equal hemispheres.

The Equator is the only line of latitude that is a great circle, as its plane passes through the center of the Earth.

All lines of longitude (meridians), including the Prime Meridian, form great circles when paired with their opposite meridians. In geographical terms, they are classified as great circles.

The Tropic of Cancer is a small circle because its plane does not pass through the center of the Earth.

Therefore, the Prime Meridian and the Equator are great circles.

Answer: 1 and 3 only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which of the following is/are cold ocean current/currents?
1. Alaska Current
2. North Atlantic Drift
3. West Wind Drift

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
The Alaska Current is a warm water current flowing northwards along the coast of British Columbia and the Alaska Panhandle.

The North Atlantic Drift is a powerful warm ocean current that continues the Gulf Stream northeast.

The West Wind Drift, also known as the Antarctic Circumpolar Current, is a cold ocean current that flows from west to east around Antarctica.

Therefore, only the West Wind Drift is a cold ocean current.

Answer: 3 only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists:
List-I (Rescue Operations carried out by the Government of India)List-II (Countries)
A. Operation KaveriI. Israel
B. Operation IndravatiII. Haiti
C. Operation AjayIII. Ukraine
D. Operation GangaIV. Sudan

Code:
questions.solution:
Operation Kaveri was launched by the Government of India to evacuate Indian citizens from Sudan.

Operation Indravati was launched to evacuate Indian nationals from Haiti.

Operation Ajay was launched to evacuate Indian citizens from Israel.

Operation Ganga was an evacuation mission to bring back Indian citizens from Ukraine.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

Answer: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which of the following statements with reference to Sleet is/are correct?
1. Sleet is frozen raindrops and refrozen melted snow-water
2. It occurs when a layer of air with the temperature below freezing point overlies a warm layer near the ground surface

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
Sleet is defined as frozen raindrops and refrozen melted snow-water. Thus, statement 1 is correct.

For sleet to form, a layer of warm air (above freezing point) must overlie a subfreezing layer of air near the ground. Snow falls through the warm layer, melts into rain, and then refreezes into ice pellets as it passes through the cold layer near the ground. Statement 2 incorrectly states that a freezing layer overlies a warm layer near the ground. Thus, statement 2 is incorrect.

Answer: 1 only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following latitudes will experience a minimum angle of the Sun's rays when it is Summer Solstice in the Northern Hemisphere?
questions.solution:
During the Summer Solstice in the Northern Hemisphere, the Sun is directly overhead at the Tropic of Cancer (23.5^{}^{\circ}$ N). The angle of elevation of the Sun's rays decreases as the latitudinal distance from the Tropic of Cancer increases.

Let us calculate the latitudinal distance of each given option from the Tropic of Cancer:
Arctic Circle (66.5^{}^{\circ}$ N): $66.5^{}^{\circ} - 23.5^{}^{\circ} = 43^{}^{\circ}$
Equator (0^{}^{\circ}$): 23.5^{}^{\circ} - 0^{}^{\circ} = 23.5^{}^{\circ}$
Tropic of Cancer (23.5^{}^{\circ}$ N): 0^{}^{\circ}$
Tropic of Capricorn (23.5^{}^{\circ}$ S): 23.5^{}^{\circ} + 23.5^{}^{\circ} = 47^{}^{\circ}$

Since the Tropic of Capricorn is at the maximum latitudinal distance from the Tropic of Cancer among the given options, it will experience the most slanted rays, and thus the minimum angle of the Sun's rays.

Answer: Tropic of Capricorn

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Temperate forests of South India, known as 'Sholas' are found in which of the following hills?
1. Anaimalai
2. Nilgiris
3. Palani

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
Sholas are patches of stunted tropical montane evergreen forests found in valleys separated by rolling grasslands in the higher elevations of South India.

These forests are primarily found in the higher altitude regions of the Western Ghats, specifically in the Nilgiris, Anaimalai, and Palani hills.

Therefore, Shola forests are found in all the three given hills.

Answer: 1, 2 and 3

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one among the following is NOT included in the National Food Security Mission Commercial Crops (NFSM-CC)?
questions.solution:
The National Food Security Mission - Commercial Crops (NFSM-CC) is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at enhancing the production and productivity of specific commercial crops.

The crops covered under the NFSM-CC are Cotton, Jute, and Sugarcane.

Coffee is a plantation crop and is managed by the Coffee Board under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Therefore, it is not included in the NFSM-CC.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements with regard to a steel plant:
I. It was setup in 1964 with Russian collaboration
II. It receives iron ore from the Rourkela region
III. Water and Hydel power is supplied by the Damodar Valley Corporation

Identify the Steel Plant on the basis of the above facts:
questions.solution:
Bokaro Steel Plant was set up in 1964 with Russian collaboration.

It was established on the principle of transportation cost minimisation by creating the Bokaro-Rourkela combine. It receives iron ore from the Rourkela region and the wagons on return take coal to Rourkela.

Water and hydel power are supplied by the Damodar Valley Corporation.

Answer: Bokaro Steel Plant

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: An offshore terminal at Vadinar has been developed to reduce pressure from which of the following major ports in India?
questions.solution:
Vadinar is a coastal town located in the Devbhumi Dwarka district of Gujarat.

An offshore oil terminal was developed at Vadinar to reduce the congestion and pressure on the Kandla Port, which is a major port also located in Gujarat.

The terminal primarily handles crude oil imports and is operated by the Deendayal Port Authority (formerly Kandla Port Trust).

Answer: Kandla Port

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: As per the India State of Forest Report 2021, which one of the following Himalayan states has the highest percentage of its geographical area under forest?
questions.solution:
According to the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2021, the percentage of geographical area under forest cover for the given states is as follows:

Arunachal Pradesh: $79.33\%$
Sikkim: $47.08\%$
Uttarakhand: $45.44\%$
Himachal Pradesh: $27.73\%$

Arunachal Pradesh has the highest percentage of its geographical area under forest cover among the given options.

Answer: Arunachal Pradesh

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which of the following statements with reference to L-Wave or Long Wave generated by an earthquake is/are correct?
1. They follow the Earth's circumference
2. They travel at more or less at a constant rate

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
L-waves or Long waves are surface waves generated by an earthquake.

They travel along the surface of the Earth, which means they follow the Earth's circumference. Thus, statement 1 is correct.

Unlike body waves (P and S waves) whose velocities increase with depth due to the increasing density and rigidity of the Earth's interior, L-waves travel through the relatively uniform surface layers (crust). Therefore, they travel at a more or less constant rate. Thus, statement 2 is also correct.

Both statements 1 and 2 are correct.

Answer: Both 1 and 2

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is formed when volcanic ash is carried by running water and is deposited as a sedimentary layer?
questions.solution:
Volcanic ash consists of fine particles of fragmented volcanic rock and glass. When this ash is carried by running water and deposited as a sedimentary layer, it undergoes compaction and cementation over time.

The lithified rock formed from the consolidation of volcanic ash is known as tuff. Basalt is an extrusive igneous rock, lapilli refers to small volcanic fragments, and slate is a metamorphic rock.

Answer: Tuff

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Chronologically arrange the following political events related to Indian National Movement beginning from the earliest:
1. Formation of Swaraj Party
2. Communal Award
3. Lucknow Pact
4. Simla Conference

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
The chronological order of the given political events is determined by the years in which they occurred:

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Condensation of water vapour into water is influenced by which of the following factor/factors?
1. Volume of air
2. Humidity
3. Temperature

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
Condensation is the process of transformation of water vapour into liquid water, which is primarily caused by the loss of heat.

Condensation depends upon the amount of cooling and the relative humidity of the air. It is influenced by the volume of air, temperature, pressure, and humidity.

Condensation takes place under the following conditions:
1. When the temperature of the air is reduced to the dew point with its volume remaining constant.
2. When both the volume and the temperature are reduced.
3. When moisture is added to the air through evaporation.

Thus, volume of air, humidity, and temperature all influence the condensation of water vapour.

Answer: 1, 2 and 3

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about 'REJUPAVE' is correct?

Answer: It's an indigenously developed road construction technology at high altitudes

questions.subject: General Ability

questions.solution:
The Nobel Peace Prize for the year 2002 was awarded to Jimmy Carter for his decades of untiring effort to find peaceful solutions to international conflicts, to advance democracy and human rights, and to promote economic and social development.

Woodrow Wilson received the prize in 1919 for his role in founding the League of Nations.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which of the following statements with reference to Coriolis force is/are correct?
1. Coriolis force acts perpendicular to the pressure gradient force
2. At the equator, the Coriolis force is zero and the wind blows perpendicular to the isobars

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
The Coriolis force acts perpendicular to the pressure gradient force. The pressure gradient force is perpendicular to an isobar, while the Coriolis force acts perpendicular to the wind direction. As a result of these forces operating perpendicular to each other, the wind blows around low-pressure areas instead of directly into them.

The magnitude of the Coriolis force is directly proportional to the sine of the latitude angle (\sin \phi$).

At the equator, the latitude is \phi = 0^{{}^{\circ}}$. Since $\sin 0^{{}^{\circ}} = 0$, the Coriolis force is zero at the equator.

Due to the absence of the Coriolis force at the equator, there is no deflection of the wind. Consequently, the wind moves directly from high pressure to low pressure along the pressure gradient force, which means it blows perpendicular to the isobars.

Therefore, both the given statements are correct.

Answer: Both 1 and 2

The Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE), a laboratory of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), has developed the Kaveri aero-engine. questions.solution:
The Self-Respect Movement was founded by E. V. Ramaswami Naicker (commonly known as Periyar) in 1925 in Tamil Nadu. Its aim was to achieve a society where backward castes have equal human rights, and to encourage backward castes to have self-respect in the context of a caste-based society.

ahmanas.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which of the following statements about the Home Rule League are correct?
1. Lokamanya Tilak set up the Home Rule League at the Bombay Provincial Conference held at Belgaum in April 1916
2. Annie Besant announced the formation of Home Rule League in September 1916
3. To avoid friction, Tilak's League was to work in Maharashtra (excluding Bombay city), Karnataka, Central Provinces and Berar and Besant's League was given charge of the rest of India
Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
Lokamanya Tilak set up the Home Rule League at the Bombay Provincial Conference held at Belgaum in April 1916. This statement is correct.

Annie Besant announced the formation of her Home Rule League in September 1916 at Madras. This statement is correct.

To avoid friction and overlapping of work, the two leagues divided their areas of operation. Tilak's League was assigned Maharashtra (excluding Bombay city), Karnataka, Central Provinces, and Berar. Annie Besant's League was given charge of the rest of India, including Bombay city. This statement is also correct.

Since all three statements are correct, the correct option is 1, 2 and 3.

Answer: 1, 2 and 3

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar is NOT correct?
options: He was the Principal of Sanskrit College, Calcutta
He was a Government Inspector of Schools
He was a Secretary to the Bethune School
He was the founder of Widow Remarriage Association
questions.solution:
Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was appointed as the Principal of Sanskrit College, Calcutta in 1851.

He served as a Government Inspector of Schools for South Bengal in 1855.

He was closely associated with the Bethune School and served as its Secretary.

The Widow Remarriage Association was founded by Vishnu Shastri Pandit and Mahadev Govind Ranade in Maharashtra, not by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar. Although Vidyasagar played a crucial role in the passing of the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act of 1856, he did not found the Widow Remarriage Association.

Therefore, the statement that he was the founder of the Widow Remarriage Association is not correct.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: As per the Annual Report 2023-24 of the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, which of the following states are the major producer of Copper in the country?
questions.solution:
As per the Annual Report of the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, the major producers of copper ore in the country are Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.

Madhya Pradesh is the largest producer of copper in India, primarily from the Malanjkhand copper project, contributing to more than half of the country's production. Rajasthan is the second-largest producer, known for the Khetri copper belt. Jharkhand also produces copper but in much smaller quantities compared to Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.

Answer: Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: As per the Land Revenue Records, any land is categorized as Culturable Waste-Land if it is left fallow (uncultivated) for more than
questions.solution:
According to the Land Revenue Records in India, land use categories are defined based on the duration for which the land is left uncultivated.

Current fallow land is left uncultivated for one or less than one agricultural year.

Fallow land other than current fallow is left uncultivated for the past 1 to 5 agricultural years.

Culturable waste-land is defined as any land which is left fallow (uncultivated) for more than 5 agricultural years. It can be brought under cultivation after improving it through reclamation practices.

Answer: 5 years

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Arrange the following foreign travellers to India in chronological order, beginning with the earliest:
1. Peter Mundy
2. Antonio Monserrate
3. Afanasii Nikitich Nikitin
4. Ibn Battuta
Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
Ibn Battuta was a Moroccan traveller who visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq in the 14th century (1333-1347).

Afanasii Nikitich Nikitin was a Russian merchant who visited the Bahmani kingdom in the 15th century (1466-1472).

Antonio Monserrate was a Portuguese Jesuit missionary who visited the court of Akbar in the 16th century (1578-1582).

Peter Mundy was an English traveller who visited India during the reign of Shah Jahan in the 17th century (1628-1633).

The correct chronological order is 4 - 3 - 2 - 1.

Answer: 4 – 3 – 2 – 1

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: With which of the following was the Bretton Woods System NOT associated
options: Economic recovery after the Second World War
International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
Establishment of a monetary system based on floating exchange rate
questions.solution:
The Bretton Woods System was established in 1944 to rebuild the international economic system after the Second World War.

It led to the creation of two major international institutions: the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD, now part of the World Bank).

The system was based on fixed exchange rates, where currencies were pegged to the US dollar, which was in turn pegged to gold. It did not establish a monetary system based on floating exchange rates.

Therefore, the establishment of a monetary system based on floating exchange rates is not associated with the Bretton Woods System.

Answer: Establishment of a monetary system based on floating exchange rate

options: the capital city of the Cheras
questions.solution:
Senguttuvan, also known as Cheran Senguttuvan, was a prominent king of the Chera dynasty during the Sangam period in ancient South India.

He is famously celebrated in the ancient Tamil epic Silappatikaram, which is attributed to his brother, Ilango Adigal.

Therefore, Senguttuvan is the name of a Chera king.

Answer: a Chera king

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The Ramacharita, an example of dvyasrya-kavya, telling two stories simultaneously, was written by
questions.solution:
The Ramacharita is a Sanskrit epic poem written by Sandhyakara Nandi during the Pala Empire.

It is an example of dvyasrya-kavya, which means it tells two stories simultaneously. Through wordplay (slesha), the poem narrates the story of the Hindu epic Ramayana and the life of the Pala king Ramapala at the same time.

Answer: Sandhyakara

questions.solution:

Due to severe drought, the Indo-Pak war of 1965, and the Sino-Indian war of 1962, the Indian economy was in a weak state. The government declared a "Plan Holiday" and the Fourth Five-Year Plan was delayed.

During this period, three Annual Plans were implemented from 1966 to 1969.

Hence, the years of the Annual Plans were 1966-1969.

Answer: 1966-1969

questions.solution:
Pitt's India Act of 1784 established the Board of Control to guide and control the work of the Court of Directors and the Government of India. This act created a system of double government, where the Court of Directors managed commercial affairs, while the Board of Control managed political affairs.

Answer: Pitt's India Act of 1784

Therefore, neither statement 1 nor 2 is correct.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which of the following rights under the Constitution of India is/are Fundamental Right(s)?
1. Right to work
2. Right to privacy
3. Right to free and compulsory education in the age bracket of six to eighteen years
Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is incorrect. The Right to work is a Directive Principle of State Policy under Article 41 of the Constitution of India, not a Fundamental Right.

Statement 2 is correct. The Right to privacy is recognized as a Fundamental Right under Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) following the Supreme Court's landmark judgment in the K.S. Puttaswamy case.

Statement 3 is incorrect. The Right to Education under Article 21A provides for free and compulsory education to all children in the age group of six to fourteen years, not six to eighteen years.

Therefore, only statement 2 represents a Fundamental Right.

Answer: 2 only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements with regard to flags of International Organizations:
1. The flag of EU has a circle of gold stars on a white background
2. The Flag of the UN carries two pairs of olive tree branches
3. The ASEAN flag carries blue, red, white and yellow colours
How many of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is incorrect. The flag of the European Union features a circle of twelve gold stars on a blue background, not a white background.

Statement 2 is incorrect. The flag of the United Nations features a map of the world inscribed in a wreath consisting of two crossed olive branches (which is one pair, not two pairs).

Statement 3 is correct. The ASEAN flag has a blue background with a red circle in the center, outlined in white, containing ten yellow paddy stalks. Thus, it carries blue, red, white, and yellow colours.

Therefore, only one statement is correct.

Answer: 1

The Abhijit Sen Committee (2002) was associated with formulating a long-term food grain policy, not with Panchayati Raj institutions.
